name: b-flash-digicam-funfair
prompt: Late-night fairground snapshot from roughly 2003, the kind of picture a mate grabbed with a little silver compact digicam set to its slow-sync party mode: the pop-up flash blasts the foreground while the shutter lingers open long enough for the background to swim. Dead centre, framed from the knees up and caught from a touch below, a figure in a plain charcoal hand-knitted ski mask and chunky grey woollen gloves stands squarely facing the camera, eyes calm and level in the openings, the knit smooth, unpatterned and evenly flash-lit so the face area reads clean and bright. One glove grips an oversized puff of candy-pink candyfloss on a stick, the other lets a knotted see-through bag of water hang down with one small orange goldfish inside, a prize from a stall. The pose is stiff and courteous, like a guest humouring whoever shouted cheese. The flash flattens and slightly overcooks the figure and throws a crisp short shadow, but its reach dies within a couple of metres: behind, the spinning waltzer and the bulb-framed rides dissolve into looping squiggles of hot pink, acid green, amber and cobalt, shaken into zigzags by an unsteady hand, set against a sky of inky black peppered with blotchy red and green sensor grain. Saturated, slightly crunchy early-CCD colour, a bluish cast from the flash, violet halos bleeding off the brightest bulbs, soft corners, horizon tilted a few degrees. Awnings and stall fronts are bare, unmarked canvas, and the picture carries no writing, numbers or emblems of any kind. Thanks.
